transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Erin (Acme Security Eng), Marcus (Acme Platform), Jill (Acme Compliance)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
- Discussed SSO/SAML integration, SCIM provisioning, RBAC/least-privilege model and audit/logging expectations.
- Customer currently on Okta, interested in customer-managed keys + VPC options.
- Action items: send security artifacts, SAML metadata, schedule RBAC walkthrough.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Erin: Yep yep, loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:06] Sophie: Great. So quick intros — I'm Sophie, AE, and Daniel here is our solutions engineer.
[00:11] Daniel: Hi all. We'll focus this session on SSO/SCIM and RBAC best practices and how Redwood maps to least-privilege models.
[00:18] Marcus: Thanks. From Acme side, Marcus platform lead, Erin is our security engineer and Jill does compliance.
[00:25] Jill: hi, thanks. we have a checklist from legal too so we'll probably jump to audit logs and KMS.
[00:30] Sophie: Perfect, that fits. Quick question — what's your IdP today?
[00:33] Erin: We're on Okta for most of the company, and using SCIM for provisioning into internal apps. We also have some teams on Azure AD but Okta is the canonical.
[00:41] Daniel: Okay Okta is covered by our SAML 2.0 and SCIM v2 integrations. We support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO flows.
[00:48] Erin: Great. Two main items we care about: 1) we need automated provisioning and group sync (so we can enforce least-privilege), and 2) audit trails for who did what and when.
[00:58] Daniel: Absolutely. For provisioning we expose SCIM endpoints and you can map groups to roles. Typical pattern is: Okta groups -> SCIM group -> Redwood RBAC role (e.g., org-admin, app-admin, deployer, viewer).
[01:10] Marcus: Are there pre-built mappings for common roles or do we have to create everything manually?
[01:14] Daniel: We ship a recommended role schema in the docs — basic roles plus a few finer-grained ones for model ops. It's configurable; you can create custom roles and then attach permissions.
[01:23] Erin: What permission granularity do you support? Like can we separate model deploy permissions from billing or log access?
[01:28] Daniel: Yes — permissions are scoped to resource families. Examples: model.deploy, model.rollback, route.manage, billing.view, audit.view. You can attach them to roles.
[01:36] Jill: And can SCIM sync also provision service accounts or just users?
[01:40] Daniel: SCIM is user and group focused. For service accounts we recommend creating machine/service principals in the console and then using credential rotation with KMS integration — or you can create a dedicated Okta service account that maps to a Redwood service principal via SCIM if you prefer.
[01:52] Erin: On encryption: can you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault? We need BYOK for certain datasets.
[02:00] Daniel: Yes — we support CMKs for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted accounts we offer platform-managed encryption by default but we have an enterprise option for customer-managed keys; that requires a private deployment or a dedicated tenancy depending on the requirement.
[02:12] Marcus: When you say "Private" do you mean VPC peering or on-prem?
[02:15] Sophie: Both options exist. Private offers a customer-managed control plane and VPC peering; on-prem is available for air-gapped customers. Dedicated is reserved capacity within our cloud with stronger tenancy and optional KMS integration.
[02:27] Jill: For our auditors, we need proof of SOC 2 and ISO 27001. Do you have those artifacts?
[02:32] Sophie: Yes, we'll send the attestation reports and the security whitepaper. We'll redact as needed.
[02:36] Erin: Good. How about log retention and export? We need to ship logs to our SIEM (Splunk).
[02:41] Daniel: We publish admin and audit logs with a retention default of 90 days on hosted, and longer for Dedicated/Private. We provide a streaming export: APIs + S3 export + direct integration to SIEMs. We can push to your S3 or set up an event stream.
[02:54] Marcus: Is there an append-only audit log? Tamper-evidence?
[02:58] Daniel: For Dedicated/Private we support immutable storage options and can integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption. For hosted we maintain integrity controls and attestations in the SOC 2; if you need tamper-evidence we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[03:12] Jill: What about SCIM attribute mappings — we need department, cost_center and manager chain in the token so RBAC can be enforced per-team.
[03:20] Daniel: SCIM v2 supports custom attributes. Our schema allows you to map Okta attributes into group metadata and to populate role membership. We have an example SCIM schema in the guide (I'll share).
[03:29] Erin: Can role changes via SCIM be immediate? We need near real-time revocation when someone is offboarded.
[03:36] Daniel: SCIM push events are near real-time; typically within a few seconds to a minute depending on IdP polling. We also accept SAML assertions for session control. For absolute immediate revocation, you can revoke tokens via the API and we have session invalidation endpoints.
[03:49] Marcus: How do you handle cross-account/tenant RBAC? We have multiple business units that should not see each other's models.
[03:55] Daniel: We support multi-tenant isolation at the org level. You can model business units as separate orgs or projects with strict role boundaries; shared models can be handled via a publish/approval flow.
[04:05] Erin: About permissions — do you have default least-privilege templates?
[04:09] Sophie: Yes, we provide starter templates: Read-only viewer, Developer (deploy + run), Ops (deploy + rollback + route management) and Admin. They are recommended to get you started, then you can tighten further.
[04:20] Jill: For compliance we also need retention policies for prompts and transcript data. Do you store customer prompts and responses?
[04:27] Daniel: By default we retain request/response logs for troubleshooting and billing. For Dedicated/Private you can opt out of request logging or set shorter retention windows. For hosted we offer configurable retention and an option for zero retention for certain customers on enterprise plans. We'll document the options in the artifact we send.
[04:44] Erin: Is there PII redaction support? We have PHI in some calls and need automatic redaction in logs.
[04:50] Daniel: We provide tools for token-level redaction and a configurable pipeline to scrub PII before it lands in long-term logs. For PHI workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with additional redaction configured.
[05:00] Marcus: For SAML metadata exchange — what's the required fields and do you supply metadata XML?
[05:05] Daniel: Yes we'll provide SP metadata XML. Minimum fields: entityID, ACS URL, certificate, and single logout URL if you use SLO. We support signed assertions and encrypted NameID.
[05:16] Erin: For nameid we prefer persistent, not transient. Also team attributes need to be in SAML or SCIM?
[05:21] Daniel: Best practice is groups via SCIM and persistent NameID for identity. We can accept group claims in SAML but SCIM is the source of truth for group membership.
[05:30] Jill: Audit question — do you include admin console changes in the audit log? For example role creation, permission changes?
[05:35] Daniel: Yes, admin actions, role changes, permission grants, and policy updates are all captured. We also version role definitions so you can see history.
[05:44] Erin: Who has access to security logs on Redwood side? We need to know separation of duties for support access.
[05:50] Sophie: Support engineers have scoped access and it's logged. For customer-facing support we use ephemeral access with just-in-time, and all access is logged and requires approval. For Dedicated/Private you can restrict vendor access completely.
[06:01] Marcus: If we go Dedicated, how does key rotation work? We need to rotate CMKs quarterly.
[06:06] Daniel: With CMK we integrate with AWS KMS rotation policies or Azure Key Vault rotation. For Dedicated we can automate rotation and we support key rewraps with minimal downtime. We'll provide runbooks.
[06:18] Jill: Do you undergo penetration tests and can you share summary results?
[06:22] Sophie: Yes we do annual pen tests and we can share executive summaries under an NDA; the SOC 2 also covers vulnerability management.
[06:31] Erin: Regarding data residency — we need EU-only hosting for certain projects. Do you have region controls?
[06:36] Daniel: Yes, region pinning is supported. For hosted we have EU regions and you can pin your org to EU; Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[06:44] Marcus: One concern — if we use SCIM to map Okta groups to roles, how do we prevent privilege escalation via group nesting?
[06:51] Daniel: We recommend flattening critical groups and using explicit deny rules for sensitive permissions. Our SCIM implementation can be configured to ignore nested groups or to resolve nesting per your policy. We'll show config options in the guide.
[07:03] Erin: Can you log SAML assertions for troubleshooting?
[07:06] Daniel: We can log SAML exchanges for debug but those logs are sensitive; they are access controlled and can be redacted. We recommend capturing them only during troubleshooting windows.
[07:14] Jill: For our audit trail we need an exportable CSV of every admin action for the last 2 years. Is that feasible?
[07:20] Daniel: For Dedicated/Private yes; for hosted we typically expose up to 1 year by default but can extend for enterprise. Exports via API or S3 are supported.
[07:28] Sophie: All right I want to make sure we're capturing next steps — we'll send the docs and metadata, Daniel will provide SCIM schema, and we'll schedule the RBAC walkthrough.
[07:36] Marcus: Sounds good. Also we'll confirm whether we need CMK or just SaaS-managed keys for the pilot.
[07:41] Erin: One last question: Do you support SCIM delta syncs or only full replaces?
[07:46] Daniel: We support delta for Okta; most IdPs do. It's much more efficient for big orgs.
[07:52] Jill: ok thank you, that addresses most of our checklist.
[07:55] Sophie: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:58] Erin: Thanks all.
[08:00] Meeting ends.
